evidence_boundary: This ledger records a source-level semantic review of lessons, worked answers, case studies, exercises, worksheets, rubrics, and lab guides. It verifies named mechanisms against bounded primary or official sources, distinguishes normative course contracts, and does not turn synthetic examples into production measurements.

location.heading: Mechanism: a boundary buys independence and creates an interface

claims.claim: A module can hide implementation without adding a network or a new operator. A deployable service buys independent rollout and scaling, but adds partial failure, compatibility, telemetry, authorization, and on-call work. An event boundary buys time and failure decoupling only when the producer's fact, the consumer's lag tolerance, replay semantics, and authority are explicit.
source_sections: Read the complete article; record three boundary drivers, two reasons to remain modular, and one extraction threshold.
claims.scope_limit: This verification is limited to the mechanism and failure assumptions stated in the lesson; examples and lab values are synthetic unless explicitly identified as measured evidence.

location.heading: Mechanism: interfaces are maintained by conversations

claims.claim: Conway's observation is predictive, not prescriptive: systems tend to reflect communication structures because an interface cannot remain coherent without communication among its designers and operators. A service boundary imposed across teams that must coordinate every change creates a distributed monolith.
source_sections: Read the author page and linked original paper; map three required technical interfaces to their human communication paths.

location.heading: Mechanism: promotion is a decision over comparable evidence

claims.claim: Shadow traffic copies an input to a candidate while the old path remains authoritative. Remove or isolate irreversible effects. Normalize nondeterminism before comparison: timestamps, ordering, generated IDs, and tolerated precision. Measure population, coverage, mismatch classes, latency, freshness, resource use, and cost. A small global mismatch percentage can hide a complete failure for one tenant or operation, so segment results.
